lots.guide_summary: A$30-80, all SOLD Gowans hammers for sterling heart padlock bracelets (8 close or same-item results, Oct 2025 to Aug 2026, mostly $45-80). No UNSOLD found. Two eBay asks (A$190, A$295) are snippet-only leads and not counted. Plain weight-matched sterling bracelets at Gowans ran $45-120 (category guide). Melt floor: 23.4g x 0.925 = 21.65g fine x A$2.635/g (XAG US$57.37/oz at api.gold-api.com 2026-10-21, USD/AUD 1.4286 open.er-api.com) = about A$57 before refiner discount; a scrap buyer would pay perhaps A$40-45. Melt is a floor, not a sale. No currency conversion in the sold entries.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD in 24 months = $50 hammer (Gowans 427182, heart padlock sterling bracelet, Aug 2026). 50 / 1.198 = 41.74, rounded down to $40 (all-in $47.92, below melt of about $57). Flip: likely resale about $70 (Gowans 375088 $80, 373330 $70, 427182 $50, weight-matched 406344 $60). Selling on eBay AU: fees about 13.4% ($9.38) and tracked small-parcel postage about $10, net $50.62. 50.62 / 2.396 = 21.13, rounded down to $20. Margin is thin; this is mainly a keep or a cheap silver buy near melt.
lots.confidence_reason: 925 mark read and style clear, and there are several same-type Gowans SOLD results whose API data and photos I viewed, but none of the comps has a stated weight and none is a single gate bracelet; lot 53's weight is not checkable from photos.
lots.condition: Surface scratches and wear on padlock and links (visible in photo 2); links appear intact; safety chain present.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 shows '925' in a rectangular cartouche on the heart padlock back; no other legible marks. Photo 1 shows a classic gate bracelet with engraved heart padlock and safety chain. Identification confirmed.
lots.question_for_gowans: Does the 23.4g include the padlock and safety chain; are there any hallmarks on the links or padlock besides 925 (e.g. a British lion or date letter); does the padlock spring shut and hold, and are all gate links sound?

Retail asks (Rubyglint guide about A$196 for a pale 2.5ct, AfricaGems pair A$1,200) are category guides only and not counted. USD converted at 1.4286 (open.er-api.com, 2026-10-21).
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD in 24 months = $80 hammer (Gowans 425668 oval 3ct, and 441777 oval 3.5ct, both look like lot 60). 80 / 1.198 = 66.78, rounded down to $65 (all-in $77.87). Flip: likely resale $80 (the repeated Gowans hammer; I do not count the $240 outlier). eBay AU fees 13.4% ($10.72) and letter-post with tracking about $8, net $61.28. 61.28 / 2.396 = 25.58, rounded down to $25. Both figures assume the stone is natural aquamarine as described; if it is blue topaz it is worth about $10-30.

Enlarged crop shows a light greenish-blue oval with a pale centre (window), consistent with commercial aquamarine but equally with topaz. lots.question_for_gowans: Has the stone been tested or weighed (actual carat weight and mm size), is 'natural aquamarine' the consignor's claim or tested, and are there any chips on the girdle?
